claim: The Neotropics are the most biodiverse region on Earth, home to at least a third of global biodiversity.

evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Raven et al., 2020.

claim: The Neotropical region includes 8 of the world's 34 biodiversity hotspots.
source: This region not only includes the largest tropical rainforest, Amazonia, but also 8 of the world's 34 biodiversity hotspots (Mittermeier et al., 2011).

We did not find evidence to reject the null hypothesis of equal diversification, with similar diversity dynamics (Sc. 1–4) found across the biogeographic units of Neotropical evolution identified here (Figure 6, Table 2).
